cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to all in Rome who are loved by God (Romans 1:1, 7). He just finished a chain that had me HOPPING on my gold base: those God called, He justified, and those He justified, He glorified (Romans 8:30). Now Paul stops and asks, "What then shall we say in response to these things?"

cards.question: Paul's next line starts with "If God is for us…" What does Paul say follows from that?

answers.text: No one can stand against us
We must earn His help first

cards.text: Then Paul points to the biggest gift there is: God did not spare His own Son but gave Him up for us all. Friend, I once guarded my last bag of chocolate chips like it was the crown jewels, and God gave up His SON.

cards.question: God already gave up His own Son for us all. So what does Paul say God will also do?

answers.text: Ask us to pay Him back
Hold back the rest for now

cards.text: Friend, if somebody hands you the keys to the WHOLE bakery, you don't stand there sweating about one sprinkle. Then Paul asks, "Who will bring any charge against God’s elect?"

cards.question: Who will bring any charge against God's elect? What answer does Paul give?

answers.text: Their good works speak for them

cards.text: Next Paul asks, "Who is there to condemn us?" He points to Christ Jesus, who died, and more than that was raised to life, and is at the right hand of God, and friend, the best line on MY résumé is "sold for a quarter."

cards.question: At the right hand of God, Paul says Christ Jesus is ___ for us.

cards.text: Now Paul asks the big one: "Who shall separate us from the love of Christ?" Then he rattles off a list that keeps going like a receipt that won't STOP printing: trouble, distress, persecution, famine, nakedness, danger and sword.

cards.question: Paul lists trouble, distress, persecution, famine, nakedness, danger and sword. What kind of things are on that list?

cards.text: Then Paul quotes the Scriptures (Psalm 44:22): "For Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered." Heavy line, friend, the kind that makes even my oven go quiet.

cards.question: True or false: after that whole list, Paul says trouble, famine or sword can separate us from the love of Christ.
In all those hard things, what does Paul say we are through Him who loved us?

cards.text: Then Paul says, "For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor principalities, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers," and he's STILL not done. I lose count naming my own six toppings, and this man is covering angels, powers and the FUTURE.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the future might someday be able to separate us from God's love.
Paul adds height and depth. Then he says nothing else in all ___ will be able to separate us from the love of God.
True or false: Paul ends by saying this love of God is found in Christ Jesus our Lord.

findings.problem: The setup says only that Christ Jesus died, was raised to life, and is at God's right hand. It gives the baker no basis for choosing "interceding" over "waiting" or "watching," so the blank asks them to guess wording they have not seen rather than reason out the meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
